newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania T-bill issue oversubscribed, yields down.
newsitem.headline: Romania T-bill issue oversubscribed, yields down.

text.p: An issue of 82.05 billion lei in Romanian three-month treasury bills was heavily oversubscribed with bids by 11 banks exceeding by 400.37 billion lei the finance ministry's offer, a central bank (BNR) statement said on Wednesday.
The T-bills placed through a Dutch style auction on Tuesday, offer an annual yield of 65 percent, down from the previous 90 percent.
The bids ranged from 59 to 82 percent, the BNR data showed.
Some 66 percent of the issue was bought by commercial banks operating in Romania, including branches and subsidiaries of foreign banks, while the rest was bought for their corporate clients.

Operators said returns were sliding down in line with a gradual relaxation in the BNR's monetary policy, which pushed down short-term money market rates to around 75 percent this week, from 90 percent over the past weeks.
They also said Tuesday's T-bill issue had not been sufficient to drain excess leu funds from the money market.

Traders forecasted fresh lows of the money market rates due to the excess of liquidity caused by the BNR's repeated purchases of dollars to counteract the effects of foreign currency inflows in the local capital markets.
